newsitem.title: UK: Device explodes near British soldiers in N.Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Device explodes near British soldiers in N.Ireland.

text.p: An explosive device was set off near patrolling British security forces in the Irish nationalist stronghold of west Belfast on Thursday but no serious injuries were reported, security sources said.
No organisation immediately claimed responsibility for the attack.
A police spokesman said that just after 1300 gmt "some form of explosive device was detonated" at Glenaleena Road in Ballymurphy, a sprawling Catholic housing estate.
"There was a joint police and army patrol in the area at the time. There are no reports of any serious injuries," the spokesman said.
Irish Republican Army guerrillas fighting to end British rule have stepped up armed actions since October, killing two British soldiers in bomb and sniper attacks.
